excerpts.text: This is the original NeXT [computer](/entity/m01m3v) used by [Sir Tim Berners-Lee](/entity/m07d5b) to design the World Wide Web and host the first web page at the European laboratory for particle physics, CERN, in December 1990. In March 1989 Tim Berners-Lee wrote a document on “Information Management: A Proposal” for colleagues at CERN. His boss, Mike Sendall, described the proposal as ‘vague but exciting…’ and, in 1990, approved the purchase of the NeXT computer.

excerpts.text: In March 1989 [Tim Berners-Lee](http://www.w3.org/People/Berners-Lee/) at [CERN](http://public.web.cern.ch/public/), Geneva, Switzerland, issued *[Information Management: A Proposal](http://www.w3.org/History/1989/proposal.html), proposing an Internet-based hypertext system.*In his words, this was a "an attempt to persuade CERN management that a global hypertext system was in CERN's interests. Note that the only name I had for it at this time was 'Mesh'." This document represents the conceptual origin of the World Wide Web.
